subject: Numeracy
title: Our day: morning, afternoon, night
subtopics: What comes first and next in our day
objectives: Children will tell morning from night using pictures and routines.
Children will say what happens first and next in the school day with support.
content: Telling morning, afternoon and night apart using familiar routines and pictures, and saying what happens first and next.
teachingActivities: Link each time word to a clear daily event; use picture cards in order; refer to the routine each day using the time words.
learnerActivities: Sort day and night pictures, order the school day with picture cards, act out routines and sing a day song.
resources: Picture cards: waking up, eating breakfast, school, lunch, nap, dinner, bedtime
assessment: Check whether children sort day and night pictures and name one thing that happens in the morning.
expectedOutcomes: Sorts day and night pictures correctly.
Names one activity that happens in the morning.

lessons.title: Day and night
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will tell day pictures from night pictures using the sun and the moon.
successCriteria: Points to the sun for day and the moon for night
Says morning or night with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know the daily routine at school and can use first, next and words such as morning and sleep in simple talk.
resources: A large sun picture and a large moon picture
Picture cards of day activities (playing outside, breakfast) and night activities (sleeping, stars)
lessons.starter: Show the sun and say "When the sun is up, it is day." Show the moon and say "When the moon is up, it is night." Ask "What do we do at night?"
teacherActivities: Place the sun picture and the moon picture on the mat. Hold up one card and say "Breakfast. Is it day or night?"
Hold up a card of a child sleeping and ask again.
Let each child choose a card and place it under the sun or the moon.
Act out waking up in the morning and going to sleep at night.
learnerActivities: Children point to the sun for day.
Children point to the moon and say "night".
Child places the card and says "day" or "night".
Children stretch for the morning and curl up for night.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Place the sun picture and the moon picture on the mat. Hold up one card and say "Breakfast. Is it day or night?" Children: Children point to the sun for day.
Step 2. Teacher: Hold up a card of a child sleeping and ask again. Children: Children point to the moon and say "night".
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child choose a card and place it under the sun or the moon. Children: Child places the card and says "day" or "night".
Step 4. Teacher: Act out waking up in the morning and going to sleep at night. Children: Children stretch for the morning and curl up for night.

practical.title: Sun and moon sort
steps: Lay the sun and moon on the floor.
Children sort picture cards under the sun or the moon.
practical.safety: Use large cards with rounded corners; children walk to place cards and do not run.

differentiation.support: Offer two cards at a time, one clear day and one clear night.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to name something they do when the sun is up and something they do when the moon is up.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is breakfast in the day or the night?
What do we do at night?

expectedOutcomes: Says morning or night with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to the sun and moon. Say "Good morning, sun. Goodnight, moon."
lessons.homeConnection: Talk with your child about what happens in the morning and what happens at night.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "tell day pictures from night pictures using the sun and the moon" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: The moon and a sleeping child
learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Sun is up, wake up, wake up. Moon is up, sleep, sleep, sleep.

lessons.title: Morning, afternoon, night
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will place pictures in three groups: morning, afternoon and night.
successCriteria: Places a picture in the correct time group
Says one of the three time words
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know the daily routine at school and can use first, next and words such as morning and sleep in simple talk.
resources: Three large paper circles labelled with a rising sun, a bright sun and a moon
Picture cards for breakfast, lunch and bedtime, plus playing and nap pictures
lessons.starter: Show three circles: a rising sun, a high sun and a moon. Say "Morning, afternoon and night. These are three parts of a day."
teacherActivities: Hold up the breakfast card and say "Morning." Place it under the rising sun.
Hold up the lunch card and say "Afternoon." Place it under the bright sun.
Hold up the bedtime card and say "Night." Place it under the moon.
Give each child a card and ask them to place it in a group.
learnerActivities: Children say "morning" and watch.
Children say "afternoon".
Children say "night".
Child chooses a group and places the card.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Hold up the breakfast card and say "Morning." Place it under the rising sun. Children: Children say "morning" and watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Hold up the lunch card and say "Afternoon." Place it under the bright sun. Children: Children say "afternoon".
Step 3. Teacher: Hold up the bedtime card and say "Night." Place it under the moon. Children: Children say "night".
Step 4. Teacher: Give each child a card and ask them to place it in a group. Children: Child chooses a group and places the card.

practical.title: Three part day
steps: Each child sorts picture cards into the three groups.
Tell a friend what they did.
practical.safety: Use large cards; keep the sorting area clear of obstacles.

differentiation.support: Use morning and night only until the child is secure.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell what comes between morning and night.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is lunch in the morning or the afternoon?

expectedOutcomes: Sorts routines into morning, afternoon and night
lessons.conclusion: Sing the day song and put the cards away.
lessons.homeConnection: Name the part of the day when you eat meals at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "place pictures in three groups: morning, afternoon and night" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: First and next in our day
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: What comes first and next in our day
objectives: Children will order three picture cards of the school day and say first and next.
successCriteria: Puts two or three cards in order
Says first or next with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know the daily routine at school and can use first, next and words such as morning and sleep in simple talk.
resources: Picture cards: arrive at school, play, wash hands, snack, home time
A string line on the floor
lessons.starter: Say "What do we do first at school? What do we do next?" Show the picture of arriving at school and say "First!"
teacherActivities: Put the "arrive" card at the start of the string line. Say "First."
Place the "play" card next and say "Next, we play." Then "wash hands" and "snack".
Mix the cards and ask a child to put them in the right order.
Act out the routine: walk in, play, wash hands, eat, wave goodbye.
learnerActivities: Children say "first".
Children say "next" and point to each card.
Child places the cards from first to last.
Children act each part in order.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put the "arrive" card at the start of the string line. Say "First." Children: Children say "first".
Step 2. Teacher: Place the "play" card next and say "Next, we play." Then "wash hands" and "snack". Children: Children say "next" and point to each card.
Step 3. Teacher: Mix the cards and ask a child to put them in the right order. Children: Child places the cards from first to last.
Step 4. Teacher: Act out the routine: walk in, play, wash hands, eat, wave goodbye. Children: Children act each part in order.

practical.title: Our school day line
steps: Lay a string line on the floor.
Place the picture cards in order.
Walk along the line saying first, next, last.
practical.safety: Fix the string with tape; children walk one at a time with an adult beside them.

differentiation.support: Use only three cards and place the first card for the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell the order without the cards.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do first at school?

lessons.conclusion: Walk the line one last time and wave goodbye at the end.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about what you do first, next and last when getting ready for school.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "order three picture cards of the school day and say first and next" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: My day story
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: What comes first and next in our day
objectives: Children will listen to a story about a day and say what happens in the morning, afternoon and night.
successCriteria: Says one thing that happens in each part of the day
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know the daily routine at school and can use first, next and words such as morning and sleep in simple talk.
lessons.starter: Hold up the soft toy and say "This is Kemi. Let us hear about Kemi’s day. Listen for morning, afternoon and night."
teacherActivities: Tell the first part and act it: wash face, eat breakfast. Place the sun card.
Tell the second part and act playing. Place the bright sun card.
Tell the last part and act brushing teeth and sleeping. Place the moon card.
Ask "What did Kemi do first?" and "What did Kemi do at night?"
learnerActivities: Children copy the actions and say "morning".
Children play and say "afternoon".
Children pretend to brush teeth and say "night".
Children answer with a word or action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Tell the first part and act it: wash face, eat breakfast. Place the sun card. Children: Children copy the actions and say "morning".
Step 2. Teacher: Tell the second part and act playing. Place the bright sun card. Children: Children play and say "afternoon".
Step 3. Teacher: Tell the last part and act brushing teeth and sleeping. Place the moon card. Children: Children pretend to brush teeth and say "night".
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What did Kemi do first?" and "What did Kemi do at night?" Children: Children answer with a word or action.

practical.title: Act Kemi’s day
steps: Give each child a toy or doll.
Put the toy to bed at the end.
practical.safety: Use soft toys; place a blanket on the floor; children move gently.

differentiation.support: Act only the morning part and say the words together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell the story in their own words using the cards.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What did Kemi do in the morning?
When did Kemi go to bed?

expectedOutcomes: Names events in morning, afternoon and night
lessons.conclusion: Say "Goodnight, Kemi" together and tuck the toy under the blanket.
lessons.homeConnection: Tell your child a story about their own day at bedtime.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "listen to a story about a day and say what happens in the morning, afternoon and night" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.story: In the morning, Kemi woke up. She washed her face and ate her breakfast. In the afternoon, Kemi went to school and played with her friends. At night, Kemi had her supper. She brushed her teeth and said goodnight. Kemi closed her eyes. Goodnight, Kemi.

lessons.title: Time of day stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show they know day and night and the order of the day at three stations.
successCriteria: Puts routine cards in order with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know the daily routine at school and can use first, next and words such as morning and sleep in simple talk.
lessons.starter: Sing the day song and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask "Is this day or night?" and "What comes next?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station.
Child answers and places cards.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Is this day or night?" and "What comes next?" Children: Child answers and places cards.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Keep cards large; supervise stations; keep walkways clear.

differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to explain the order of the day.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: sorts day and night; names morning events; orders routine pictures.

questions.question: Is it day or night when we sleep?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 2
Understands parts of the day with support
lessons.conclusion: Sing the day song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Use morning, afternoon and night words in talk at home.
